references.text: God promises to be with Moses' mouth and teach him what he should say; the same promise is now also given to Aaron.
Moses shall put the words in Aaron's mouth, and Aaron shall speak to Pharaoh as Moses' prophet.
God promises to put His words in the prophet's mouth, the same expression used regarding Aaron.
The Lord puts His words in His servant's mouth, parallel to how God sets the words in Aaron's mouth.
The Lord touches Jeremiah's mouth and places His words there, the same action as with Aaron.
The Lord put a word in Balaam's mouth, the same expression for divine inspiration.
Balaam must hold fast to what the Lord puts in his mouth, parallel to Aaron's commission.
Jesus promises that the Holy Spirit will give the disciples the words they should speak, the same divine guidance.
The Holy Spirit will teach the disciples what they should say, parallel to God's promise to teach Moses and Aaron.
Jesus promises to give the disciples mouth and wisdom, the same type of divine help as given to Moses and Aaron.
A strong thematic parallel regarding God's solution to Moses' burden: the sharing of the Spirit (Numbers) and the sharing of the gift of speech (Exodus).
